column3: “Having a skin disease” is rendered “a leper,” and “house of separateness” as “a separate house.”
The Hebrew קָבָלְ־ עָם (“before the people,” possibly a place name) is rendered “before the people.”
“Descendants of the fourth” is rendered “Your sons to the fourth generation.”
“A month of days” is rendered “one month.”
NASB supplies “to him” and “therefore.” Some ancient versions read “Tappuah” for “Tiphsah.”
“To be his hands with him” is rendered “so that his hand might be with him,” and “in his hand” as “under his rule.”
“Fortress” is rendered “castle,” and “sons of the Gileadites” as “the Gileadites.”
“Took into exile” is rendered “carried them captive.”
